name: Putrid Claw
summary: Putrid Claws are the decaying hands severed from mindless undead prowling the woods west of Brill. Deathguard Dillinger collects them as definitive proof that the encroaching Scourge threat near the old bridge is being held at bay.

sections.title: Trophy of the Mindless
sections.body: Even in their own homeland, the Forsaken are not entirely safe from the Lich King's reach. Pockets of mindless Scourge—rotting dead and ravaged corpses—regularly wander across the eastern borders into Tirisfal Glades, clustering along roads and near the old bridge west of Brill. To ensure the safety of travelers and garrison supply lines, the Deathguards place bounties on these wandering horrors. A severed putrid claw serves as unmistakable, physical evidence that one more shambling corpse has been put down for good.

faq.q: What are putrid claws used for?
faq.answer: Deathguard Dillinger stationed in Brill collects them as bounties to confirm that local Forsaken recruits are thinning out the Scourge wandering Tirisfal Glades.

faq.q: Where do putrid claws come from?
faq.answer: They are harvested from the rotting dead and ravaged corpses roaming the haunted woods west of Brill, particularly near the old river bridge.

faq.q: Why is the Scourge in Tirisfal Glades?
faq.answer: Following the devastation of Lordaeron, remnants of the Lich King's mindless Scourge continuously trickle westward across the borders into Tirisfal, menacing roads and settlements unless actively culled.

faq.q: Why don't the Forsaken just let the mindless undead wander?
faq.answer: Unlike the Forsaken, who broke free under Queen Sylvanas and regained their will, the mindless Scourge obey only dark instincts or the Lich King's lingering command, attacking any living or free undead on sight.

angles.text: For fresh Forsaken initiates leaving Deathknell, clearing these mindless Scourge is an early reminder that liberation comes with constant defense against the mindless husks they once resembled.
